tasks.short: Review the flight plan, weather and notices before flight, agree route and fuel with dispatch, choose altitudes and speeds in flight, and request route or level changes from air traffic control.

steps.what: Airline pilot reviews the flight plan, weather and notices to airmen before flight
Airline pilot agrees the route and fuel with dispatch
Airline pilot gathers wind and turbulence reports for the route ahead
Airline pilot chooses altitudes and speeds in flight for the safest and smoothest flight
Airline pilot requests route or level changes from air traffic control

tasks.design: The briefing package on the flight-deck tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}) filters notices to airmen by route, altitude and time by rule and puts closures and runway notices first; no notice is hidden, all remain one tap away. In flight, wind and turbulence updates arrive on the tablet, so altitude choices take less asking around. Agreeing the route with dispatch, choosing altitudes and talking with air traffic control stay with the pilots.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pilots read long, unsorted lists of notices and asked others about ride conditions by radio.
tasks.enabler_now: Briefing apps filter notices by route and time; datalink brings weather updates.
tasks.still_hard: A critical notice can still hide in plain text.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a lower level to spare passengers turbulence despite the fuel cost.

reach.learn: Whether pilots query plans less often.

evidence.claim: EUROCONTROL has an AI module that ranks notices to airmen; operators check 600 to 800 a day and about 1.5% need a system update; live use not stated.
Lido Flight 4D plans routes, profiles and fuel against weather and airspace restrictions, with digital notices.

assumptions: Boundary: from the briefing package to the change cleared; flight planning by dispatch is outside.
Input contract: notices and weather from the operator's briefing service; fallback is the full printed package.
Agreeing routes and talking with air traffic control do not change.
The filter rules are approved by flight operations.
Pricing of s3: about half of gathering is asking dispatch and air traffic control for reports, which the tablet updates replace; listening to the frequency and own observation do not change.
research_questions: Do pilots miss fewer relevant notices?

incremental.description: Airline pilot reports notices the filter placed wrongly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short routes with few notices; high: long routes over busy airspace.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold the crew briefing, read the crew list and notes, direct the first officer and cabin crew during flight, and debrief the crew.

steps.what: Airline pilot holds the crew briefing before flight
Airline pilot reads the printed crew list and flight notes
Airline pilot directs activities of aircraft crews during flights
Airline pilot debriefs the crew after flight

tasks.design: The crew app on the tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the crew, their positions, special passengers and flight notes in one view, instead of printed lists. Briefing, directing and debriefing the crew stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Crew lists and notes were printed and collected before each duty.
tasks.enabler_now: Crew apps show crew lists and flight notes on tablets.
tasks.still_hard: Crews often meet for the first time at the briefing.
tasks.human_edge: Setting a calm tone that lets a junior crew member speak up.

evidence.claim: Crew apps can show crew lists, positions and flight notes on tablets.

assumptions: Boundary: from the crew list to the crew debriefed; crew rostering is outside.
Input contract: crew list from crew control; fallback is printed lists.
Briefing, directing and debriefing do not change.
Crew members' time does not change.
research_questions: Do briefings start on time more often?

incremental.description: Airline pilot checks the crew app is synced before the briefing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an operator already on tablets; high: an operator moving from printed lists.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write block times, fuel and distances in the journey log, record flight times in the personal logbook, check the entries, hand the journey log to operations, and correct mismatches with crew control.

steps.what: Airline pilot records flight times, distances flown and fuel consumption in the journey log
Airline pilot records flight times in the personal log book
Airline pilot checks the log entries
Airline pilot hands the journey log to operations
Airline pilot corrects mismatches with crew control

tasks.design: Out, off, on and in times and fuel figures sent by the aircraft fill the electronic journey log on the tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the personal electronic logbook takes actual times from the crew system. The pilot checks the entries, and once checked the journey log syncs to operations. Flight time records are kept 24 months and used for flight time limits, not to rate pilots.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times, distances and fuel were written by hand in two logs.
tasks.enabler_now: Aircraft send block times and fuel by datalink; electronic logbooks read crew system data.
tasks.still_hard: Diversions and aircraft swaps leave gaps the pilot must fill.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a logged time cannot be right for the route.
tasks.altitude: The pilot checks logs instead of writing them.

evidence.claim: Aircraft send out, off, on and in times and fuel figures by datalink that can fill electronic logs.
Actual flight, duty and rest times are kept 24 months.
Logs that tie times and fuel to named pilots can check performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from flight data to corrected mismatches; flight time limit planning is outside.
Input contract: times and fuel from the aircraft datalink; crew data from crew control; fallback is handwriting.
Checking the log stays with the pilot.
The authority approves the electronic journey log.

incremental.description: Airline pilot fills gaps after diversions and aircraft swaps.

approvals.approved_version: The log entries as checked by the pilot in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: aircraft without datalink times; high: all aircraft sending times and fuel.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the training session, instruct trainees during line training flights, debrief them, write the training report, and send it to the training department.

steps.what: Airline pilot prepares the training session
Airline pilot instructs other pilots and student pilots in aircraft operations during line training
Airline pilot writes the training report on a paper form
Airline pilot hands the training report to the training department

tasks.design: Briefing material per training phase sits in the training system ({LMS}), so the trainer prepares from a shared set. The training report is an electronic form with the competency grades and short remarks; once the trainer has completed and signed it, it goes to the training department. Instructing and debriefing stay with the trainer; no software grades the trainee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions were prepared from personal notes and reports filled on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Training systems hold briefing material and electronic report forms.
tasks.still_hard: Good line training depends on the day's weather and traffic.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when to let a trainee make a small mistake and learn from it.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Training systems can hold briefing material and electronic report forms with competency grades.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in vocational training is high-risk under Annex III point 3; here no software grades the trainee.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training syllabus to the report filed; the check ride is outside.
Input contract: syllabus from the training department; fallback is personal notes and paper forms.
Instructing and debriefing do not change.
research_questions: Are reports complete at first submission?

incremental.description: Airline pilot syncs the report after an offline flight.

approvals.approved_version: The training report as completed and signed by the trainer in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: occasional training flights; high: a trainer with many line training flights.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The airline pilot keeps choosing routes and altitudes, leading the crew and training others; sorting notices, printed lists, handwritten logs and paper reports shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A pilot with more attention for flying and teaching.

job.title: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers
